attackResults.designSmuggling: FAIL IN PART. Selecting Option B is a legitimate coordinator preference, and the in-memory invocation-bound doctor record already exists in doctor v4. The draft goes beyond the actor boundary by making the required host-effect truth table optional while inventing an explicit-cancel consequence without a commit/outcome rule; see ADV-D032-02 and ADV-D032-03.
attackResults.joinBlockerDisposition: FAIL. The draft does not claim the join is closed, but 'stated not waved' is false: the component-tail journal-versus-FC-RO blocker remains unmentioned, permissionRef is left as an unresolved disjunction, and host effect-outcome/enforcement-disclosure/cancel semantics are not routed to a mandatory successor; see ADV-D032-03.
attackResults.optionAFairHearing: FAIL IN PART. The rejection names Option A's costs but omits its strongest benefit: one durable monotonic authorization, effect-commit, revocation, and audit regime for both host and component effects.
attackResults.optionCFairHearing: FAIL IN PART. The draft calls C 'split every class' even though the measured decomposition has two wholly host classes and two split classes, and D-032 itself adopts those two component tails. It omits C's actor-fidelity benefit; see ADV-D032-05.
attackResults.permissionVocabularyMinting: PASS narrowly. D-032 mints no PT-* token, status token, or DR-105 truth-table cell. It does create a host authorization regime, which is the decision's subject, but that regime is incomplete rather than hidden; see ADV-D032-02.
attackResults.d000Clause3Completeness: FAIL. Alternatives exist and the entry is marked PREFERENCE-LADEN, but there is no readiness-effect statement, no reversibility class, and no temporal overturn rule for conforming successors; see ADV-D032-04.
attackResults.sourceAndStandingHonesty: FAIL. The operative citations target doctor-contract.v2 even though v2 was independently rejected and D-035 has recorded v4 as DR-114's accepted design contract. The join verdict is a v1/v1 pair review, while the draft presents its findings beside v2 without describing the lineage; see ADV-D032-01.
attackResults.hostActorOwner: FAIL. The heading promises a named owner, but the clause names an authorization carrier and three governing surfaces, not an accountable owner. It also omits the joint DR-105/DR-114 owners that doctor v4 ID-DEP-12 names as deciders; see ADV-D032-02.

objections.claim: D-032 is based on the current DR-114 design-contract lineage and accurately states the standing of every subject it constrains.
objections.evidence: Lines 15 and 62-64 name doctor-contract.v2, say it remains a candidate, and require successors to conform. The current register says v2 was independently REJECTED at four measurement blockers, v3 was rejected at one accounting blocker, and doctor-contract.v4 is the accepted DR-114 design contract under ADOPTED D-035, at df2e717555616db096e61548458f23b442f7f0e37b2d2461eabc2c33201e94b3 with ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at zero blockers. V4 carries the routed actor question, the Option-B costs, the reserved permissionRef/effectOutcome/enforcementDisclosure members, and the exact component-tail decomposition. The cited join verdict 538f3681... itself reviewed permission v1 against doctor v1, not v2 or v4. A decision aimed at rejected v2 neither dispositions current v4 nor explains which historical findings survive its repairs.
objections.proposedFix: Rebase the decision on doctor-contract.v4 and D-035, pin v4 and its accepted verdict, and name permission-truth-tables.v1 at its measured digest and actual candidate standing. Describe 538f3681... honestly as the v1/v1 join review whose root actor finding is carried forward by v4, not as a current v4 join verdict. State exactly which v4 members a conforming successor withdraws, retains, or fills.

objections.claim: Option B names an accountable host-actor owner and leaves host effects fail-closed until a complete, reviewed host authorization regime exists.
objections.evidence: The 'Host-actor owner' clause names the invocation as authorization origin and lists DR-123, DR-114, and file 03 as governing sources; none is an accountable owner role. Doctor v4 ID-DEP-12 routes the decision to the coordinator jointly with DR-105's Security + platform owners and DR-114's Operability + security owners, but D-032 records no joint-owner participation or successor owner. More seriously, line 45 says a host-effect truth table may be added later 'if product wants one.' Option B removes host actions from DR-105's requested/granted/denied, effect-commit, revocation, and audit machinery; those semantics cannot become optional while the same clause declares invocation/policy a sufficient authorization origin. The draft does not say host consented actions remain UNEXERCISABLE until an owner-recorded, independently reviewed host regime lands.
objections.proposedFix: Name the accountable host-authorization owner and the required joint DR-105/DR-114 authorities. Make a scoped host-effect authorization contract mandatory, not optional, before any CA-1 head, CA-2, CA-3, or host CA-4 action becomes exercisable. Require it to preserve file-03 authorization/confinement honesty, cancellation/effect-commit ordering, outcome disclosure, CI policy, audit, and fail-closed behavior, with independent review. State that D-032 itself authorizes no host effect.

objections.claim: Every surviving join blocker is either discharged by the actor choice or explicitly retained and routed; none is waved by calling a DR-105 concept inapplicable.
objections.evidence: First, BLK-4 survives on the component tails D-032 deliberately keeps in DR-105: DR-105 journals every accepted component request, while doctor's FC-RO fixture forbids writes outside Operational metadata and DR-124 has not assigned the journal a state class. Doctor v4 ID-DEP-7 preserves this exact collision, but D-032's blocker list omits it. Second, doctor v4's Option-B cost requires a disposition for where unknown/completed-before-cancel host effect outcomes land and what carries enforcement disclosure. D-032 merely says DR-105's INDETERMINATE and COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION are grant-journal outcomes, which does not describe the same physical facts when a host egress or spawned tool crosses an irreversible boundary and doctor cannot tell what happened. Third, 'permissionRef stays permanently reserved or is withdrawn' is not a decision, and 'explicit cancel' supplies no linearization, effect-commit, cleanup, or post-report rule. The current join is therefore not made coherent, and the residuals are not all routed despite the 'stated not waved' heading.
objections.proposedFix: Enumerate all seven historical blockers against current v4 and mark each DISCHARGED, REPAIRED-IN-V4, or STILL-ROUTED with owner and evidence. Route the component-tail grant-journal/FC-RO collision to DR-124 and keep those tails non-closing until it lands. Choose withdrawn versus reserved for permissionRef. Define or mandatorily route typed host effect outcomes, enforcement disclosure, explicit-cancel/effect-commit ordering, cleanup, and audit; retain v4's fail-closed unpopulated-reserved-member behavior until those successors are accepted. Commission a fresh v4/permission-successor join review before either row closes.

objections.claim: D-032 satisfies D-000 clause 3 with an explicit readiness effect, reversibility class, and an overturn procedure that remains true after conforming successors land.
objections.evidence: The draft has no Readiness effect section at all. It therefore does not say whether the actor decision moves DR-105, DR-114, their join, condition 2, or any candidate standing. Its only reversibility text is 'Supersession + revert of C-D032'; no class is stated. Yet Decision 6 commands future permission and doctor successors to conform. Once either successor lands, reverting C-D032 cannot undo that successor or restore the prior unresolved actor regime, so the one-revert statement is only true before dependents. D-000 requires readiness/reversibility/overturn to be recorded rather than inferred.
objections.proposedFix: Add 'Readiness effect: zero' unless a separately reviewed register-content change is intended; say explicitly that no row, join verdict, candidate standing, or blueprint authorization moves. State the reversibility class as total only before a dependent successor lands. Afterward, supersession is prospective and every conforming successor remains until its owning authority separately supersedes or reverts it. Require each successor to name D-032 and carry rollback.

objections.claim: Options A and C receive a fair strongest-case hearing before Option B is selected.
objections.evidence: Option A is described only by its costs, omitting its principal benefit: one durable monotonic grant/effect-commit/revocation/audit model and one typed outcome/disclosure vocabulary across host and component effects. Option C is called 'split every class at the actor line,' but doctor v4's measured decomposition says CA-2 and CA-3 are wholly host-actor while only CA-1 and CA-4 split; D-032 itself preserves precisely those two component tails, so the chosen solution is already a B+C hybrid. Option C's benefit—matching authorization to the actual actor without forcing host heads into component tokens—is not stated. A preference-laden rejection should weigh those gains against complexity, not list only burdens.
objections.proposedFix: Record the strongest benefit and full cost of each alternative. Describe the selected shape honestly as Option B for host heads plus Option C's measured component-tail split. Explain why losing A's monotonic cross-actor journal and accepting the hybrid's two regimes is the better trade under the named owner and mandatory host-regime plan.
